309	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
310	
311	The major2 comparison result (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
312	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
313	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
314	
315	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
316	|---|---|---|---|---|
317	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
318	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
319	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
320	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
321	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
322	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
323	
324	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
325	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
326	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
327	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
328	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
329	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
330	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
331	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
332	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
333	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
334	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
335	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
336	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
337	
338	**Evidence for presence.** The fingerprint population is the union of B and
339	all admitted E0–E4 results, including fingerprints present only in a pivot.
340	A known matched finding establishes presence even when waived; waiver status
341	is a separate axis. Absence of a particular fingerprint requires complete
342	subject enumeration, determinate `emitWhen` proof roots for every selected
343	subject, and that fingerprint absent from the exact admitted emission set.
344	A known finding on another subject does not invalidate this negative knowledge.
345	All-false roots establish the stronger claim that the rule emitted no findings.
346	Required execution deficiencies still affect the overall Run and comparison
347	verdict; they do not retract a determinate per-rule fingerprint result.
348	An advisory `pass` alone does not establish absence. A false root may retain
349	unknown child witnesses under the published three-valued composition law;
350	those witnesses do not turn a determinate false root into unknown. Unknown
351	roots, incomplete enumeration, disabled evaluation and exhausted budgets do
352	not establish a negative result. Known hits remain usable in a partial result.
353	
354	E1–E3 preserve current non-substituted inputs: selected source, configuration,
355	provider/toolchain contexts, imports, native facts and Coverage, subject
356	inventories, attribution/search records and candidate-producer evidence.
357	Plan-bound envelopes are compared by their retained semantic contents after
358	removing only the explicitly substituted parent locators. A policy, scope or
359	waiver remint cannot authorize replacement of native evidence. E0 uses the
360	prior detector and its admitted dependencies over current source and can
361	therefore have different native contexts and evidence. Snapshot membership
362	alone is not proof that native extraction examined a path; a counterfactual
363	requiring evidence outside the attested extraction extent is unavailable.
364	
365	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
366	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
367	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
368	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
369	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
370	
371	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
372	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
373	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
374	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
375	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
376	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
377	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
378	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
379	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
380	non-gating delta.
381	
382	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
383	
384	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
385	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
386	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
387	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
388	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
389	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
390	
391	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
392	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
393	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
394	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
395	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
396	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
397	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
398	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
399	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

403	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
404	
405	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
406	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
407	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
408	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
409	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
410	
411	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
412	|---|---|---|
413	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
414	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
415	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
416	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
417	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
418	
419	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
420	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
421	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
422	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
423	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
424	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
425	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
426	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
427	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
428	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
429	
430	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
431	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
432	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
433	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
434	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
435	
436	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
437	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
438	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
439	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
440	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
441	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
442	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
443	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
444	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
445	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
446	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
447	but never feeds a predicate.
448	
449	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
450	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive

451	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
452	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
453	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
454	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
455	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.
456	
457	**A repair evidence requirement over one of these two relations has its own
458	owning outcome law**, `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law`
459	(§6). It is separate from native §4.6 because these relations mint no `fact2` and
460	carry no Coverage, and **each kind is projected through its own payload**: a
461	runtime requirement reads `observability`, `observationWindow` and
462	`observedPopulation`; a history requirement reads `revisionRange` and
463	`collectionScope`, which are its bounds fields; `HistoryPayloadV1` also carries
464	subjects and has no runtime observation-window, population or observability
465	fields. Neither kind may report the other's outcomes.
466	
467	**A repair target is a fingerprint, not a path, and the join is published.**
468	`RepairPlanDescriptor.targets` are `finding-key2:` **fingerprints**, while
469	`RuntimeSubject` is keyed by `{path, symbol?}` and `HistorySubject` by `{path}`.
470	The deterministic projection is
471	`imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law/targetSubjectProjection`:
472	each target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by `evidenceRunId` (preview
473	already refuses one that is not); that `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of
474	the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention is
475	`preimage` and whose bytes are therefore re-hashed at Run closure; and its
476	`subjectKey` supplies the path and qualified name used for matching. The projection
477	does not classify the target by `kind`, whose vocabulary is not closed here. A
478	runtime row matches on path and, if it names a symbol, on qualified name; another
479	symbol's row does not match. A runtime row with no symbol and every history row
480	provide **file** granularity, with `granularityWidenedToFile` disclosed in the
481	projection and successful outcome. A symbol-naming runtime row provides the
482	format's path-and-name granularity, not an exact match of the whole subject key:
483	neither format distinguishes `language`, `kind` or `discriminator`. Distinct
484	findings can therefore project to the same observation. This stated limit applies
485	to every such projection; it cannot establish execution or non-execution of a
486	particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity. More than one
487	matching subject **refuses**: an ambiguous projection is not resolved by choosing
488	one. A target with no matching subject is unsupported — never satisfied, and never
489	read as evidence of non-use.
490	
491	Five limits carry over and are enforced rather than assumed.
492	**Satisfied does not mean positive**: `observed-hit` is positive execution
493	evidence and `observable-unhit` is *bounded negative* evidence, both can satisfy,
494	and the disclosure records which did. **No imported observation establishes a
495	universal negative** — one window is not universal non-use — and imported evidence
496	can never *by itself* establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe
497	`delete`/`replace`, and it can never **improve** that gate either: the gate reads
498	only the **native** `ClosedWorldV2` records the §6 relevance rule selects from the
499	evidence Run, and no imported observation is one of them.
500	It may still be an **additional required condition** alongside an
501	already-established native basis, so it is wrong to say it never affects
502	applicability; an unsatisfied imported requirement makes an otherwise-eligible
503	plan inapplicable. **Whole-versus-partial** is decided by the requirement's
504	`completeness` field: `complete` needs every plan target supported,
505	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of
506	it for an imported requirement over plan targets is selected here** and was not
507	previously published. A target that is unobservable or outside the history
508	collection scope therefore only names the cause *more precisely when the support
509	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a
510	supported target. **Bounds are separate from support**: an insufficient observation
511	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
512	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
513	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
514	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
515	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed
516	boolean**; a non-boolean refuses, so there is no `unknown` state to default and no
517	falsy value is read as optional.
518

521	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
522	
523	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV2` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
524	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
525	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
526	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
527	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
528	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
529	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
530	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
531	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
532	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
533	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
534	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
535	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
536	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
537	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
538	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
539	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
540	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
541	
542	Glob matching follows the single [portable glob contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md): full-string, case-sensitive matching; terminal whole-segment `**` includes a filename, so `src/**` matches `src/index.ts`. The same predicate applies to policy field filters and host path scopes. Each containing contract continues to own its defaults and include/exclude combination law.
543	The compiled RuleProgramV2 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
544	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
545	The exact endpoint, native field projection and imported test-filter grammars
546	are in that policy schema and the incorporated atom contract. Identity §4 and
547	the composition contract own independent subject enumeration, complete tree
548	replay, full finding emission, waiver membership and budget semantics. Declared
549	required evidence remains distinct from retained nonblocking branch diagnostics.
550	
551	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
552	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
553	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
554	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
555	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
556	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
557	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
558	
559	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
560	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
561	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
562	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
563	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
564	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
565	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
566	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
567	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
568	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
569	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
570	
571	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
572	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
573	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
574	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
575	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
576	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
577	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
578	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
579	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
580	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
581	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
582	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
583	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.
584

587	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
588	
589	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
590	
591	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
592	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
593	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
594	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
595	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
596	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
597	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
598	`run3`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
599	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
600	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit

601	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
602	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
603	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
604	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
605	
606	**The closed-world gate reads selected native records; the descriptor carries a
607	display summary.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in
608	the plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and
609	this paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
610	decided **before** any descriptor is built, and an `imported-prepared-declared`
611	evidence origin reports `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` for the separate
612	reason that a DECLARED prepared expansion is not authority for an unsafe repair.
613	
614	**A Run holds one `ClosedWorldV2` per Coverage entry, not one per Run, so the gate
615	states which entries it reads.** `ClosedWorldV2` is a required member of
616	`ViewEntryV3` (native §4.3), keyed by `CoverageKeyV2`
617	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`,
618	`subjectScopeCommitment`), and identity §3 makes several differing entries lawful
619	in one Run: "a differing tuple is a different claim, not an overlap, which is why
620	the same subject may lawfully appear under two relations, two rungs or two
621	universes." An earlier revision of this section said the prerequisite was decided
622	against "the evidence Run's own native `ClosedWorldV2`", as though a Run held one.
623	It does not, and with several retained records that phrase did not denote. The
624	selection law is the following, and it is decided over **retained** records only.
625	
626	1. **Relevant universes.** The relevant set is the union of two published joins,
627	   and a universe in neither is **truly unrelated and does not veto**.
628	   * Every universe reached by **all matching occurrences of every target
629	     fingerprint**: `finding3.subjectId` → `subject3.universe`. All occurrences,
630	     not a representative — a `finding-key2` frame carries no universe, and the
631	     projection law that groups occurrences compares `ruleId`, subject path,
632	     kind, qualified name and detector closure but **not** universe, so one
633	     fingerprint may lawfully be matched in two universes.
634	   * Every universe that **owns an unsafe edited path**, read from the
635	     **retained selected-program census** of this Run's `EnumerationPlanV1`. That
636	     parameter is **required** for evaluator3 — absent, the evaluator refuses
637	     `EVALUATOR_REQUIRED_PARAMETER_MISSING`, and full replay re-admits it — so this
638	     is a guaranteed retained join, not a caller-selected or optional unsigned map
639	     and not filename parsing. For each binding whose `enumerator.status` is
640	     `selected`, its **applicable path census** is its own `extents[]` plus, on a
641	     candidate-only cell, its `candidateSourcePaths` — "the Plan-selected
642	     source-path census for *that* program".
643	     - A binding with a **non-null universe** whose census contains the path
644	       contributes that universe.
645	     - A **selected but unavailable** binding (`universe=null`, whose `extents`
646	       remain "populated from host membership so expected file/package paths are
647	       not lost") contributes **typed unresolved ownership**: it holds a real
648	       retained expected-ownership claim with no universe to make eligible and no
649	       Coverage to establish a closed world, so it reports
650	       `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` and **does not vanish because some
651	       other owner of the same path is closed**.
652	     - An **unselected** binding is not a selected program and is never inferred.
653	     Each extent kind is read as itself: `file` and `package` are host membership
654	     extents, `symbol` is the selected program's **code** scope. All snapshot files
655	     are therefore **not** treated as every compiler's `programRootFiles`, and a
656	     selected program whose own census does not contain the edit **stays
657	     unrelated**. Legitimate **multiple ownership is preserved** — one path
658	     analysed under two Rust targets or editions is two selected bindings with two
659	     universes, and both must be eligible.
660	   * Retained **`source-path`** subject scopes (`file`, `clones`, `vcs-change`,
661	     all `universeRule: same-only`) are unioned in as an **additional retained
662	     witness**. They are **not** the owner census and cannot certify its
663	     completeness: their `subjectKindLaw` proves those scopes *name* paths, not
664	     that they *enumerate* every selected program owning one. A selected program
665	     with no such scope in this Run owns its extent just the same — which is
666	     exactly the case the census covers, and which is reachable: a universe bound
667	     only to a symbol-kind cell, owning a path through its retained symbol extent
668	     with no file inventory and no lawful `file@enumerated` scope, is admitted.
669	     Ownership is never inferred from a path prefix, a display string, an optional
670	     sidecar or an unreferenced host observation, and never by reconstructing a
671	     path from an opaque native symbol ID — that reconstruction is separately
672	     forbidden, and the census makes it unnecessary, because the program's path
673	     extent is published directly.
674	   * Targets and edits are **separate descriptor arrays with no published
675	     correspondence**, and none is invented: each is read on its own terms and
676	     the two universe sets are unioned. No edit names a target.
677	   * If an unsafe edited path is claimed by **no** selected binding's census and
678	     **no** source-path scope, its analysing universe cannot be reconstructed, and
679	     that is reported as `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` rather than guessed
680	     or treated as vacuously satisfied.
681	2. **Selected records.** For every relevant universe, **every** retained native
682	   `coverage2` of that Run whose scope's **`sourceUniverse`** is that universe.
683	   `ClosedWorldV2` characterises the universe whose subjects were examined —
684	   `coverageTotality.matchLaw` calls totality "a claim about what THIS universe
685	   examined" — and that extent is the scope's source side, so relevance is decided
686	   on `sourceUniverse` **alone**. An entry made in an unrelated universe *about* a
687	   relevant one describes the unrelated universe and is not joined. Selection is
688	   **independent of the plan's `evidenceRequirements`**: a recipe can neither
689	   narrow it to a favourable relation or rung nor remove a conflicting record from
690	   it. Records are deduplicated by retained `coverage2` **identity**, never by
691	   relation, and **ordered on UTF-8 encoded bytes** by
692	   `relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`,
693	   `subjectScopeCommitment`, then the `coverage2` identity — that sixth member
694	   makes the order total even between two records agreeing on all five
695	   coordinates, so remedies are reproducible whatever order the caller enumerated
696	   in.
697	3. **The gate.** Eligibility is the **conjunction** of `deadCodeRepairEligible`
698	   over every selected record. It is **non-vacuous**: a relevant universe that
699	   retains no native Coverage record establishes no closed world, and an empty
700	   evidence subset is not truth — it reports
701	   `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED`. Each dissenting record contributes its
702	   own remedy naming **all six ordering members unabbreviated** — including the
703	   exact retained `coverage2` identity — plus that record's own `reasons`. Naming
704	   only relation, rung and source universe would not do: two lawfully distinct
705	   retained records can differ **only** in `targetUniverse`, only in
706	   `subjectScopeCommitment`, or only in the identity itself, and a remedy that
707	   cannot tell them apart does not name the record the reader must go and look at.
708	   So two causes remain two remedies, and two records remain two records. The
709	   conservatism is deliberate: a destructive edit is a universal negative, so one
710	   dissenting relevant record defeats it, and the scoping in step 1 is what stops
711	   an unrelated closed finding from justifying the deletion of a path analysed in
712	   an open universe.
713	
714	No new public detail code is minted: every outcome above reports the existing
715	`REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED`, and the closed registry is unchanged.
716	
717	`dynamicDispatch` is **not** a global veto and must not be read as one. Native
718	§4.5 makes dynamic-edge effects **target-relative**: `affected_targets` marks the
719	subjects a dynamic edge could reach, and §4.6 turns that into
720	`resolution-incomplete` for a universal negative **about an affected subject**.
721	So a present dynamic edge disqualifies the claims that depend on the subjects it
722	reaches; it does not by itself disqualify an unrelated target in the same Run.
723	The selection law above does not read `dynamicDispatch` at all: a selected record
724	whose `dynamicDispatch` is `present` neither defeats the boolean gate nor changes
725	the display summary, and the member stays with the native record for the
726	target-relative and per-requirement judgements that own it. Those judgements are
727	**separate** from this gate and are not merged into it.
728	The roles here are distinct and are not merged: preview **admits** each evidence
729	requirement's `relation`/`minResolution` against the registered vocabulary and its
730	relation's own ladder (`admit_atom`, which is vocabulary admission, not an
731	evidence judgement), and then **consumes** that requirement's own `satisfied`
732	value; the semantic sufficiency behind it is owned by native §4.6
733	`sufficiency_v2` and the §4.5 affected-target evidence, per requirement, and is
734	never collapsed into one flag.
735	
736	**Which vocabulary `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` carries, and when it is
737	required.** Preview admits a requirement over **either evidence plane**, so the
738	field carries the vocabulary of **that requirement's** plane and the plane is
739	decided at admission from the relation's registry membership — the same place the
740	two planes are already separated — never from the value.
741	
742	* **Native plane** — the thirteen native fact relations. The value is native
743	  §4.6's `DeficiencyV2`, named here through the drift-checked mirror
744	  `common.schema.json#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency` because this bundle
745	  resolves only its own URNs.
746	* **Imported plane** — `runtime-observation` and `history-change`. Those relations
747	  mint no `fact2` and have no Coverage entry, so `sufficiency_v2` has nothing to
748	  range over and is not asked. Their outcomes are owned by
749	  `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law` and mirrored
750	  as `common.schema.json#/$defs/ImportedRequirementDeficiency`; every member names

751	  an already-published import condition and is bound to the payload field that
752	  grounds it, and each kind reports only the outcomes **its own** payload can
753	  ground — enforced at **both** the producer and this admission (§4). The
754	  requirement record gains no field: plan `targets` supply the per-target scope
755	  through the published fingerprint projection, `completeness` decides
756	  whole-versus-partial under the reading selected in §4, and `evidenceUse` supplies
757	  required-versus-optional as a typed boolean. The bounded observation demand is
758	  owned by the **admitted recipe closure** named by `recipe.closureId` — `RecipeRef`
759	  carries no such wire field and none is claimed.
760	
761	The two vocabularies are **disjoint**, and a cross-plane value — a native
762	requirement claiming `import-unmapped-only`, or an imported one claiming
763	`resolution-incomplete` — is refused at admission, as is an outcome of the wrong
764	imported **kind**, such as a history range cause on a runtime relation. This schema
765	**deliberately leaves the authoritative registry lookup to admission**: it admits
766	either vocabulary and does not attempt to reproduce the relation registries, which
767	it could not fetch rows from in any case. That is a design choice about where the
768	authority lives, not a limitation of JSON Schema — a schema *can* branch on a
769	property's `const`/`enum` even where the base type is a broader string — and
770	duplicating a registry as schema conditionals would create exactly the drift this
771	contract set avoids elsewhere. The division is stated rather than implied.
772	
773	The value carried is the **satisfaction/deficiency projection** of its producer's
774	result, not that result: `sufficiency_v2` also returns `causes` on both branches
775	and may return `disclosures` on a failing branch. Those are producer result arrays
776	and are fields of no retained record; what is retained is the evidence the
777	evaluation read, so the projection drops nothing that was retained. Presence is **typed**: `deficiency` is **required
778	exactly when `satisfied` is false** and **forbidden when it is true**, `satisfied`
779	must be an actual boolean, and an explicit `null` is refused in both branches
780	because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Both boundaries — the
781	schema and the preview admission — decide that same law and are held equal on an
782	enumerated shape table. The field previously named
783	`D9Deficiency`, which cannot express four of the nine outcomes its only producer
784	emits — `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
785	`input-closure-incomplete` and `resolution-incomplete` — leaving three conforming
786	readings and no document choosing between them: write the D9-mapped value, which
787	is `verdict-indeterminate` for **all four** and so cannot tell
788	`resolution-incomplete` (the outcome §4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal
789	negative under `unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid` over an affected target, and the one
790	a destructive unused-code recipe turns on) from three unrelated causes; write the
791	sufficiency value and be schema-invalid; or omit the field and drop the
792	disclosure. Retyping this one per-requirement field is the correction.
793	`D9Deficiency` is **unchanged** and still carries every whole-Run and
794	comparison-step termination — three of its members name evaluation, baseline and
795	query outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce — and the public D9
796	route for a Run carrying such a requirement is still native §10's. The value is a
797	**disclosure, not an authorization**: `applicable` is false whenever any
798	requirement is unsatisfied, the exact cause is carried into that requirement's
799	unmet precondition so two different causes are two different remedies, the
800	evidence authority remains the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`, and any edit
801	to the value mints a different `repairPlanId` that no authorization names.
802	That unmet precondition is emitted once per unsatisfied requirement and carries
803	the existing `REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE` code, which here says that the
804	evidence Run cannot supply what this repair requires and asserts nothing about the
805	Run having been purged or lost — `evidence.purged` and `evidence.missing` keep
806	their own distinct meaning in query results. Preview therefore reaches that one
807	code by two routes, the retained-availability and replayable-assurance failure of
808	the first paragraph above and this per-requirement insufficiency, and the remedy
809	is what tells them apart: the retention entry's remedy names the Run-level
810	restoration that route needs, while the per-requirement entry's remedy names that
811	requirement's `relation`, `minResolution`, evidence plane and exact `deficiency`.
812	`EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` remains the typed cause carrier: no
813	per-deficiency detail code is minted, because the closed public registry is not
814	where a per-requirement outcome vocabulary belongs. An unsatisfied requirement
815	with an empty `unmetPreconditions` is **not** a conforming projection — the schema
816	alone admits that shape, and the emission is decided at admission, the same
817	division of labour already stated for the deficiency vocabulary.
818	
819	`RepairPlanDescriptor.closedWorld` is a deterministic **five-field display
820	summary** of the selected records — `deadCodeRepairEligible`, `exportsClosed`,
821	`entryPointsRecognized`, `nonliteralLoading`, `externalConsumers` — and
822	`repair.schema.json` closes it at exactly those five, so a literal copy of
823	`ClosedWorldV2`, which carries seven, is refused there. It is **not** a native
824	producer record and does not claim to be one: a fieldwise reduction over several
825	entries may combine members that no single producer emitted together. That is
826	acceptable only because the record carries **no authority**. The reduction is
827	total and fixed:
828	
829	* `deadCodeRepairEligible` is the conjunction over the selected records, and
830	  `false` when none were selected.
831	* each remaining member takes the **least-closed** value present, ordering
832	  `closed ≺ open ≺ unknown`, `all ≺ partial ≺ none`, `none ≺ present`,
833	  `none-declared ≺ possible ≺ unknown`.
834	* **absence is folded in, not hidden.** When any relevant universe retains no
835	  native Coverage, or any selected binding's ownership of an unsafe path is
836	  unresolved, the reduction additionally folds in the sentinel below, so the
837	  summary cannot read as closed while eligibility is refused for that absence.
838	
839	With nothing selected the same rule yields the **five-field least-closed display
840	sentinel**, which is exactly
841	`{deadCodeRepairEligible: false, exportsClosed: unknown, entryPointsRecognized:
842	none, nonliteralLoading: present, externalConsumers: unknown}`. It is **not an
843	"all-unknown" record** and must not be described as one: only two members are
844	`unknown`; the other three are a false boolean and the least-closed pole of each
845	of the two enums that cannot spell absence. `ClosedWorldV2` has no `unknown`
846	member for `entryPointsRecognized` (`all|partial|none`) or `nonliteralLoading`
847	(`none|present`), so their poles stand in. That is this display rule applied
848	uniformly — **not** an observation that entry points went unrecognised or that
849	nonliteral loading was seen — and widening the native enum is not this section's
850	to do.
851	
852	**The summary grants no evidence authority of its own.** **No member of it is
853	authoritative, the boolean included**; the authority is the full native selection
854	above. It is never an input to
855	the gate, which reads the full selected records including the two members the
856	summary does not carry. No edit to it can make a plan applicable, since the whole
857	descriptor is the preimage of `repairPlanId`
858	(`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) and apply requires a security
859	authorization bound to that exact `repairPlanId`, base snapshot and project.
860	Preview is a Query-class step and is **not** authorization: `applicable=true` is
861	a disclosure that the preconditions held, and trust, consent, current-snapshot
862	equality and that bound authorization are all still required at apply.
863	
864	**Create-only plans still carry a summary.** A plan with no `delete` and no
865	`replace` activates no gate, and an ineligible closed world alone adds **no**
866	unmet precondition to it. It still **reads** the selection and still **builds**
867	the five-field member — the member is `required` in the descriptor and the whole
868	descriptor is the `repairPlanId` preimage, so a create-only plan does not escape
869	the question, it only escapes the veto. It is summarised by the same reduction,
870	falling back to the **five-field least-closed sentinel above** — not an
871	all-unknown record — when the Run retains no relevant native Coverage at all, so
872	the descriptor, and therefore `repairPlanId`, is deterministic for a create-only
873	plan exactly as for any other.
874	
875	**What this changes, stated precisely.** The identity *recipe* and the descriptor
876	*shape* are unchanged: the same five member names, the same `additionalProperties:
877	false`, the same schema majors, and `repairPlanId` is still
878	`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)` over the whole descriptor. What moves is
879	the *value* this member takes, so an implementation that previously used a
880	caller-selected record may now mint a different `repairPlanId` for the same
881	request. **No equality of `repairPlanId` is claimed across different Runs**:
882	`evidenceRunId` is part of the preimage, so a different Run is a different plan
883	identity however similar its evidence. Equality holds only where every descriptor
884	input, that Run included, is identical.
885	
886	The authority stays the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`. No claim is made here
887	that a later step re-reads it — `repair verify` seals a **new** Run over the
888	freshly re-snapshotted tree (`appliedSnapshotId` → `verifiedSnapshotId`) and
889	compares remaining and net-new findings; it does not re-open the original evidence
890	Run.
891	
892	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
893	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
894	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
895	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
896	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
897	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
898	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
899	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
900	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target

901	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
902	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
903	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
904	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
905	
906	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
907	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
908	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
909	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
910	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
911	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
912	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
913	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
914	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
915	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
916	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
917	
918	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
919	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
920	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
921	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
922	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
923	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
924	and remains retained if verification fails.

928	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
929	
930	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
931	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
932	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
933	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
934	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
935	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
936	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
937	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
938	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
939	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
940	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
941	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
942	
943	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
944	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
945	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
946	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
947	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
948	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
949	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
950	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
951	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
952	are the supported alternative.

956	## 8. Command inventory, outputs and parity (AR-13 surfaces, AR-16)
957	
958	`workflows/command-inventory.v3.json` is the single intended inventory,
959	validated by `workflows/schemas/evaluator3/command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
960	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
961	
962	| Group | Commands |
963	|---|---|
964	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
965	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
966	| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
967	| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
968	| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |
969	
970	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
971	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
972	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
973	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.
974	
975	**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v3 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 3 is the parity
976	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
977	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
978	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
979	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
980	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
981	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
982	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
983	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
984	`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
985	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
986	human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or
987	substitutes null for a present verdict/deficiency. Audit adds its comparison
988	fields while preserving the current analysis result. Repair verification adds
989	applied/verified snapshot, snapshot-match, targets-remaining and net-new-findings
990	fields while preserving the fresh verification Run's findings and verdict.
991	An empty findings array is a real empty result; it is never inferred from a
992	missing projection field. Ephemeral analysis retains its existing no-Run rule:
993	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
994	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.
995	The host projection must be total over the selected command's `parityFields`
996	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
997	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
998	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
999	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
1000	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
1001	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;
1002	otherwise no RunId is invented. This classification also covers a pure reference
1003	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public
1004	termination. Actual host exception handling and renderer conformance remain
1005	DR-G17/DR-G20 implementation qualification obligations.
1006	Requesting a non-applicable format is
1007	`REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION` / `OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (2). Failure of the selected
1008	required renderer **after** a committed Run is `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` (4) with
1009	detail `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`, the `runId` in the termination, and
1010	no rewrite of the Run; failure of an optional export sink leaves `success`.
1011	
1012	**Query.** The twenty closed operations remain read-only. The current schema is
1013	`workflows/schemas/evaluator3/graph-query.schema.json` major 3. The incorporated
1014	[query projection contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/workflows/query-projection-contract.v3.md)
1015	owns the complete selection, endpoint, result, ordering, traversal, continuation
1016	and evidence-disclosure laws for `graph.neighbors`, `graph.path` and `graph.reach`.
1017	It does not replace the artifact-specific owners of the other seventeen operations.
1018	
1019	Graph requests may select `run3`, `snapshot2` or `latest`; before traversal they
1020	resolve to one concrete retained Run and an exact fact-view selection. An empty
1021	resolver domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`; ambiguity is a typed refusal. A graph
1022	response never echoes an unresolved `latest` alias as its resolved view. Endpoint
1023	identity includes the selected universe and native identity, so equal paths in
1024	different analysis universes cannot silently collapse. Results retain their fact
1025	provenance. Database row IDs and backend iteration order are not public identity
1026	or ordering rules.
1027	
1028	The bounded graph contract distinguishes a page boundary from exhaustion of the
1029	logical operation. Page size is at most 1,000; produced items at most 100,000;
1030	semantic depth at most 64; visited nodes at most 1,000,000. `maxDepth` defines the
1031	requested search distance, not an implicit promise of unbounded reachability.
1032	`completeness=required` refuses genuinely unfinished work at an operation bound
1033	with `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3); exactly reaching a limit with no owed work is
1034	not incompleteness. Best-effort reports any truncation explicitly. A continuation
1035	can page only the bounded result and never reset the work budget; its last page
1036	can remain truncated with no cursor. Total-count disclosure distinguishes an
1037	exact total from a lower bound.
1038	
1039	A continuation binds the project, concrete retained Run and fact views,
1040	operation, effective parameters, ordering and position. Publication of a newer
1041	Run cannot change that selection. Index loss permits rebuilding from the same
1042	available closure; unavailable retained evidence or incompatible continuation
1043	inputs cause the contract's typed refusal, never a switch to a newer Run.
1044	
1045	For the graph operations, traversal completion and retained evidence sufficiency
1046	are separate typed disclosures, including relevant Coverage, scope, deficiency
1047	and resolution limitations. Exhausting stored edges, returning no rows, or
1048	ending pagination cannot itself prove that no callers exist. Any such finding
1049	must retain the existing native/evaluator authority and citations. All query
1050	responses carry their owned view, evidence disclosure, availability and `advisory`;

1051	the other seventeen operations retain their existing Coverage field. `advisory` is
1052	true exactly for `comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show` and
1053	`review.brief`. The three graph operations are not advisory and do not seal a Run.
1054	
1055	The query command's required parity fields are `resolved-view`, `availability`,
1056	`truncated`, `total-items`, `termination-class` and `query-response`. The last is
1057	the **complete owner-admitted GraphQueryResponseV1**, including the full context,
1058	items and any optional termination; human, JSON and agent renderers preserve its
1059	typed content. For non-graph operations the existing Coverage field stays inside
1060	that response. Graph evidence is not reduced to a synthetic Coverage scalar.
1061	The first four scalar fields are exact projections of the response context;
1062	`termination-class` comes from the enclosing command's actual StepTermination.
1063	If the response carries termination, its entire object must equal the enclosing
1064	termination. The envelope and response must identify the same project. Missing
1065	required query disclosure follows the existing required-delivery fault law.
1066	
1067	The envelope's compact `QueryResult` remains a separate record. For graph.*,
1068	`items` is the number of rows on the current page, `truncated` equals the context
1069	flag, `advisory` is false, and `nextCursor` is present exactly when the context
1070	has the identical token. `completenessMet` is true exactly when `countBasis=exact`:
1071	the declared stored-edge operation has completed, even if further pages remain
1072	to be delivered. This is neither native closed-world evidence nor a claim that
1073	all pages were delivered. A lower-bound result therefore has
1074	`completenessMet=false`, including an intermediate page whose `truncated` flag
1075	is false. The other seventeen operations retain their owned summary semantics.
1076	The reference `workflows/query_surface_projection.v3.py` checks these joins and
1077	projects the complete response; it does not admit a Run or prove traversal.
1078	
1079	**Doctor.** `opensip doctor` produces a typed report over closures, trust, store,
1080	platform, project marker and the offline window. A produced report is `success` (0)
1081	even when defects are found (detail `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`); CI must inspect
1082	`doctor.defectsFound`. Only an unproducible report is `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (4).
1083	
1084	A `doctor` report is a **different invocation** and therefore cannot deliver the
1085	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the
1086	environment report it always was.
1087	
1088	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
1089	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
1090	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
1091	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
1092	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
1093	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
1094	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
1095	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
1096	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing
1097	code `native.capability-unavailable` (a `const`, since the record declares one
1098	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
1099	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
1100	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable
1101	notice. The collection is composed **per step** —
1102	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
1103	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
1104	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
1105	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
1106	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
1107	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in
1108	different steps. Order is the selection's own.
1109	
1110	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
1111	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field
1112	of **every** `requestClass: analysis` command — `default`, `analyze`, `fit`,
1113	`audit` and `repair-verify` — and every applicable renderer carries it: human,
1114	JSON, SARIF, HTML and agent. Because it is *declared*, it is also **required**:
1115	the host projection must be total over the command's parity fields, so a caller
1116	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
1117	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the
1118	field, and an omission is a required-delivery operational fault under the law
1119	above, never a successful partial rendering.
1120	
1121	It is **advisory** — it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control
1122	verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone `Candidate`, since published
1123	Candidate records represent actual candidates. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union
1124	and is not widened to carry it.
1125	
1126	**Failure envelopes carry their errors.** A `kind=failure` envelope requires a

1128	`domainDetail` is absent, the composition in native §10 supplies the array from
1129	the route's own detail code, and where it is present `errors` is exactly that
1130	detail so the two surfaces never disagree. Before a Plan or Run exists no run
1131	envelope is fabricated.

1135	## 9. D9 goldens and typed detail (AR-16)
1136	
1137	Exit codes are the existing table: success 0, policy-failed 1, request-rejected 2,
1138	indeterminate 3, operational-failed 4, interrupted 130. Termination branch contract
1139	(schema-enforced): success carries no error/reason/signal; policy-failed carries
1140	`runId` or `authority=ephemeral`; request-rejected/operational-failed carry
1141	`errorCode` (operational also a non-none `faultCause` from the observation:
1142	host-io, ledger-busy, ledger-corrupt, cas-link, provider-protocol, durability-commit,
1143	delivery-required, output-serialization, extension-install-io, serve-protocol,
1144	host-invariant);
1145	indeterminate carries `reasonCodes`; interrupted carries `signal` and a `runId` only
1146	when a Run was committed before the interrupt. `DomainDetailCode` is explanatory
1147	detail beside an existing code, never a termination code. Selected goldens (the complete retained set
1148	is in the inventory and exercised by the model):
1149	
1150	| Situation | Class / exit | Code | Detail / remedy |
1151	|---|---|---|---|
1152	| fresh project, providers installed | success 0 | — | DEFAULTED durable retention disclosed; no policy file written |
1153	| required provider closure not installed | indeterminate 3 | `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | `COMPONENT.REQUIRED_CLOSURE_NOT_INSTALLED` → `opensip install provider-typescript` |
1154	| installed closure bytes corrupt / unspawnable | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_BYTES_CORRUPT` / `DELIVERY.CLOSURE_UNSPAWNABLE` → `opensip doctor` |
1155	| selected renderer fails after commit | operational-failed 4 | `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` | `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`; runId retained |
1156	| optional export sink fails | success 0 | — | egress never changes a verdict |
1157	| `--ephemeral` with baseline/repair prerequisite | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` | `WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY` |
1158	| pivot closure missing / revoked / unmapped project | indeterminate 3 | `BASELINE.RECIPE_UNSUPPORTED` | `BASELINE.PIVOT_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE` / `..._CLOSURE_REVOKED` / `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` |
1159	| required evidence lost in audit | indeterminate 3 | `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` | `COMPARISON.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE` → re-import |
1160	| unmapped / corrupt import artifact | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED` / `IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT` |
1161	| duplicate waiver / imperative policy key | request-rejected 2 | `CONFIG.INVALID` | `POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER` / `POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED` |
1162	| repair preimage mismatch / source moved | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` |
1163	| recovery blocked | operational-failed 4 | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` | `REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`; journal retained |
1164	| CI interactive test consent / confinement claim | request-rejected 2 | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI` / `TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED` |
1165	| doctor report with defects | success 0 | — | `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`; inspect typed outcome |
1166	| SIGINT before / after settle | interrupted 130 / settled class | — | after-settle is never reclassified |
1167	
1168	The exact class/detail pairing is determined by the golden observation and
1169	closed schemas. Disclosure-only success details do not imply a clean doctor
1170	report or grant authority. No new D9 family is introduced.

137	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
138	
139	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
140	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
141	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
142	own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
143	exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
144	this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
145	would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
146	reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
147	four `platformId`
148	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
149	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
150	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit

151	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
152	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
153	
154	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
155	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
156	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).
